notes: Educational seed. NOT clinician-reviewed. Prefer printed lab intervals when available. Do not treat as diagnosis. v1.2.1: enforced sourced-boundaries-only band policy for reference-interval markers (hematocrit, rbc, creatinine, uric-acid, ggt, hemoglobin, serum-iron) — attention / good / attention at the primary interval endpoints; no invented fair/optimal interiors; serum iron grades on the Mayo interval with an explicit lab-specific caveat. v1.2.0: replaced nine male-derived ranges with sex-specific rows; rebuilt ferritin; removed invented total-cholesterol 180; aligned female HDL; collapsed vitamin D. 27 markers still carry 'NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW' citations; see data/SOURCES.md and data/reference-ranges/reference-data.test.ts.

sourceRefs.label: Westergren ESR upper limit for females under 50 — 20 mm/h
sourceRefs.citation: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate. StatPearls, NIH Bookshelf. Conventional Westergren upper limits: males <50y 15 mm/h, males >=50y 20 mm/h, females <50y 20 mm/h, females >=50y 30 mm/h. StatPearls itself notes the reference range should be established by the performing laboratory. A low ESR is not clinically concerning, so no lower bound is graded.

sourceRefs.label: Context — ESR has no true 95% reference interval
sourceRefs.citation: The widely quoted Miller formula (Miller A, Green M, Robinson D. Simple rule for calculating normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate. BMJ. 1983;286(6361):266) gives the maximum normal ESR as age/2 in men and (age+10)/2 in women, but the authors defined it as the value above which fewer than 2% of a normal population lies — a 98th percentile, not the 95% interval used for the other markers in this panel — and describe it as an approximation. Wetteland et al. (J Intern Med. 1996; 2,145 men and 1,765 women aged 20-90) found substantially lower limits in the elderly than Miller predicts (age 90: 19 mm/h men, 23 mm/h women, versus Miller's 45 and 50). This marker cannot be graded on the same statistical footing as the others.

sourceRefs.label: IMPORTANT — this interval is lab-specific, not population-derived
sourceRefs.citation: No large reference-interval study using CLSI methodology with sex stratification could be verified for serum iron. The available lab catalogs disagree substantially: the female lower limit ranges from 27 to 40 ug/dL and the upper limit from 139 to 190 ug/dL across Mayo, Labcorp and Quest — a spread wider than the sex difference itself. Serum iron also has large diurnal and day-to-day variation and shifts across the menstrual cycle. Ferritin and transferrin saturation carry substantially more signal about iron status.

sourceRefs.label: WHO 2020 — iron deficiency at ferritin <15 ug/L; risk of iron overload above 200 ug/L in men
sourceRefs.citation: WHO guideline on use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2020. Table 1 gives <15 ug/L for adults, and <70 ug/L where infection or inflammation is present. Recommendation 1.3: 'A ferritin concentration exceeding 150 ug/L in menstruating women and 200 ug/L in men and non-menstruating women who are otherwise healthy may indicate a risk of iron overload (conditional recommendation).' WHO states these cut-offs are based on expert opinion rather than a systematic appraisal of the literature.

sourceRefs.label: EASL 2022 — male iron-overload evaluation threshold ferritin >300 ug/L
sourceRefs.citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on haemochromatosis. J Hepatol. 2022;77(2):479-502. 'Provisional iron overload based on serum iron parameters (TSAT >45% and ferritin >200 ug/L in females and TSAT >50% and ferritin >300 ug/L in males and postmenopausal women)'. IMPORTANT: the guideline threshold also requires transferrin saturation, which this panel does not measure, so a high result here is a prompt to test further, not evidence of iron overload.

sourceRefs.label: ARUP Laboratories — adult male reference interval 30-400 ng/mL (ages 20-59)
sourceRefs.citation: ARUP Laboratories test 0070065, Ferritin, LOINC 20567-4, effective 2022-02-22. Males 20-59 years 30-400 ng/mL. Used for the lab in/out-of-range flag only. A population 97.5th percentile is not a health target, which is why the upper lab limit sits above the guideline evaluation threshold.

sourceRefs.label: Caveat — the 50-100 ng/mL band is a treatment target borrowed as a proxy, not a validated optimum
sourceRefs.citation: No guideline defines an optimal ferritin for healthy adults. The 50-100 ng/mL band is the phlebotomy maintenance target for treated haemochromatosis, endorsed concordantly by EASL 2022 ('serum ferritin can be maintained with some flexibility in the range of 50-100 ug/L'), AASLD 2011 recommendation 9, and ACG 2019. It is used here because it is the only range a guideline explicitly endorses as a good place for iron stores to sit. Ferritin is also a positive acute-phase reactant and rises with inflammation, liver disease, infection, alcohol excess and malignancy, so a mid-range value can mask true deficiency. WHO recommendation 1.4: ferritin concentration should not be used alone to identify risk of iron overload.

Table 1 gives <15 ug/L for adults, and <70 ug/L where infection or inflammation is present. Recommendation 1.3: 'A ferritin concentration exceeding 150 ug/L in menstruating women and 200 ug/L in men and non-menstruating women who are otherwise healthy may indicate a risk of iron overload (conditional recommendation).' The deficiency cut-off is shared with men; only the upper thresholds differ by sex. This row applies the menstruating-women threshold, which is conservative for women past menopause.

sourceRefs.label: EASL 2022 — female iron-overload evaluation threshold ferritin >200 ug/L
sourceRefs.citation: EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines on haemochromatosis. J Hepatol. 2022;77(2):479-502. 'TSAT >45% and ferritin >200 ug/L in females'. ACG 2019 (Kowdley et al., Am J Gastroenterol 114:1202-1218) uses the same >200 ng/mL figure for women. Note both guidelines group postmenopausal women with men at >300 ug/L, so this row is conservative for women past menopause. IMPORTANT: the guideline threshold also requires transferrin saturation, which this panel does not measure.

sourceRefs.label: ARUP Laboratories — adult female reference interval 13-150 ng/mL (ages 17-59)
sourceRefs.citation: ARUP Laboratories test 0070065, Ferritin, LOINC 20567-4, effective 2022-02-22. Females 17-59 years 13-150 ng/mL. Used for the lab in/out-of-range flag only. Note the lab lower limit (13) sits below the clinical deficiency cut-off (15), so a woman can be within the lab reference interval and still iron deficient - 'in range' and 'iron replete' are different claims.

sourceRefs.label: Caveat — the 50-100 ng/mL band is a treatment target borrowed as a proxy, not a validated optimum
sourceRefs.citation: No guideline defines an optimal ferritin for healthy adults. The 50-100 ng/mL band is the phlebotomy maintenance target for treated haemochromatosis, endorsed concordantly by EASL 2022, AASLD 2011 recommendation 9, and ACG 2019. Ferritin is also a positive acute-phase reactant and rises with inflammation, liver disease, infection, alcohol excess and malignancy, so a mid-range value can mask true deficiency. WHO recommendation 1.4: ferritin concentration should not be used alone to identify risk of iron overload.

sourceRefs.label: Common serum folate sufficiency thresholds (provisional)
sourceRefs.citation: NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW: Folate cutoffs vary; many labs use ~3 ng/mL as deficiency threshold.

sourceRefs.label: Common serum B12 sufficiency thresholds (provisional)
sourceRefs.citation: NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW: B12 deficiency cutoffs vary (~200–300 pg/mL); neurologic risk may occur higher.

sourceRefs.label: Endocrine Society 2011 25(OH)D categories — deficiency <20, insufficiency 21-29, sufficiency 30-100 ng/mL
sourceRefs.citation: Holick MF, et al. Evaluation, treatment, and prevention of vitamin D deficiency: an Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2011;96(7):1911-1930. The guideline defines a single sufficiency band of 30-100 ng/mL and notes toxicity is generally associated with levels above 150 ng/mL; it designates no sub-band of 30-100 as superior, so none is claimed here.

sourceRefs.label: Caveat — the Endocrine Society withdrew the 30 ng/mL sufficiency threshold in 2024
sourceRefs.citation: Demay MB, et al. Vitamin D for the Prevention of Disease: an Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2024. The Society no longer endorses its previously proposed definition of vitamin D 'sufficiency' (at least 30 ng/mL) and does not recommend routine 25(OH)D screening in healthy adults. The 2011 thresholds are retained here because the 2024 guideline proposes no replacement cutpoints, and are shown with this caveat rather than presented as current consensus.

sourceRefs.label: hs-CRP / CRP risk-style bands (provisional; assay-dependent)
sourceRefs.citation: NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW: Standard CRP vs hs-CRP differ. Seed treats <5 mg/L as common lab ULN with tighter lifestyle bands below.

sourceRefs.label: Common adult TSH interval with tighter optimal band (provisional)
sourceRefs.citation: NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW: Typical adult TSH ~0.4–4.5 mIU/L; pregnancy and age alter targets.

sourceRefs.label: Common morning cortisol interval (provisional; timing-critical)
sourceRefs.citation: NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW: Cortisol is time-of-day dependent. Seed assumes morning sample context only.

markers.name: Homocysteine
markers.subtitle: Amino acid linked to B-vitamin status

sourceRefs.label: Refsum et al. expert opinion — upper reference limit 12 umol/L folate-replete, 15 umol/L unsupplemented (adults 15-65)
sourceRefs.citation: Refsum H, Smith AD, Ueland PM, et al. Facts and Recommendations about Total Homocysteine Determinations: An Expert Opinion. Clin Chem. 2004;50(1):3-32. Table 6 partitions upper reference limits by age and folate-fortification status: adults 15-65 years 12 umol/L supplemented / 15 umol/L not supplemented; elderly >65 years 16 / 20 umol/L. Vitamin status moves the limit far more than sex does. A low homocysteine is not clinically concerning, so no lower bound is graded.

sourceRefs.label: Why this marker is NOT split by sex
sourceRefs.citation: Refsum et al. acknowledge a real biological sex difference and then explain why it does not drive separate limits: 'After puberty, males have higher mean tHcy concentrations than females. The gender difference in mean tHcy is ~2 umol/L, but it becomes less with increasing age, and the proportion with tHcy above a given upper reference limit is similar in adult men and women.' Their formal recommendations list separate limits for children, adults, the elderly and pregnant women — sex is absent. ARUP likewise publishes a single interval of 0-15 umol/L stated as applying to both sexes. Presenting a sex-specific homocysteine interval as consensus would misrepresent the evidence.
